explanation:
**What the grids are made of.** Every input is a mostly-empty 11×11 canvas holding a few small fragments. Each fragment contains exactly one cell of colour 5, and its other cells (one colour per fragment) sit within one step of that 5 — so each fragment fits inside the 3×3 window centred on its 5. The output is always 3×3 and has exactly one 5, right in the centre.

**How the output is built.** The 5 is a registration mark. In train pair 1 the 6 sits diagonally up-left of its 5, and in the output it is up-left of the centre; the two 7s flank their 5 left and right, and in the output they flank the centre; the three 3s lie in the row below their 5, and occupy the bottom row of the output; the two 2s lie above their 5 (one directly above, one above-right), and land at (0,1),(0,2). Pair 2 and 3 behave identically: slide every fragment so that its 5 lands on the output centre, then overlay. Cells no fragment covers stay 0 (pair 2 and 3 keep zeros at exactly the uncovered positions). The fragments never compete for the same cell.

**Applied to the test input.** Four 5s: at (2,8) with three 9s (above, left, below-left) → 9 at (0,1),(1,0),(2,0); at (4,1) with 4s up-left and right → (0,0),(1,2); at (7,6) with an 8 up-right → (0,2); at (9,3) with 2s below and below-right → (2,1),(2,2). Centre is 5, remaining cells 0.

The program: find every 5 cell, cut the 3×3 window around it, and stamp its non-background cells onto the 3×3 canvas, emitting after allocation and after each stamp.

movement.text: Pair 2 and 3 behave identically: slide every fragment so that its 5 lands on the output centre, then overlay.

Stamp the fragment whose 5 is at (3,2): slide it so its 5 sits on the centre and copy its coloured cells.
